pairs.subject: prompt-safety
pairs.evidence: lib/analysis/kg-verdict.ts:268 The KG verdict gate checks model-emitted edge endpoints and prose-cited psp:* urns against the store only when the caller passes knownIds. Without it the gate returns an unqualified ok:true, so the rule that every model-emitted id is validated against the live store is opt-in, not unconditional.

techniques.evidence: lib/analysis/kg-verdict.ts:268 The closed grammar is enforced (enums plus checkExactKeys), but id validation is skipped silently when knownIds is absent. verdict.ts:209 (knownEntityIds) and law-verdict.ts:247-248 (knownIds/knownLawRefs) have the same opt-in shape. The ok result does not say the id check was skipped.

lib/analysis/kg-verdict.test.ts:63 The test asserts that a verdict with a fabricated psp:person:999999 endpoint returns ok:true when no knownIds are passed. 'Not inspected' and 'inspected and clean' come back as the same outcome, with no recorded not-inspected marker.

lib/analysis/law-verdict.ts:257 A link-scheme allowlist on model-emitted web and bill_text citation sources (http/https only). Only this link-scheme part was checked; secret masking and markup neutralization were not checked in this context.

lib/analysis/tripwires.ts:1 These tripwires are deterministic data-invariant patterns over graph rows, not canaries planted in a prompt. No prompt is assembled in this context, so there is nowhere to plant a canary.
lib/analysis/language-gate.ts:14 The persist-time and render-time gates import one TypeScript rule set, so the boundary does not cross a language and the two-runtime precondition does not hold.
